_note: My expected outcome per case, written by hand after reading every document, BEFORE running the tool on all ten. Where reviewing the tool's reasoning changed my mind, the original answer is kept in `original` with the reason in `revised_because`, so the revision is visible rather than quietly folded in. `also_acceptable` lists defensible alternatives. `tier` is the minimum attention level the tool should flag.

CB-2025-0001.why: Signed Royal Mail delivery to SW4 7QR on 24 Mar, before the 18 Apr chargeback; addresses match; AVS Y.

CB-2025-0002.why: Delivered to M1 7DR, billing is M14 5RT, AVS N, 3DS only attempted, left in a safe place with no signature. Issuer says the address is not theirs. Ambiguous by design; the tool must flag it, not decide it.

CB-2025-0003.why: 4837 needs any two: AVS Y + CVV M (req 1) and 3DS authenticated (req 2) are both documented in the gateway log.

CB-2025-0004.why: The internal fraud report is the merchant's own risk score; it meets none of the four requirements. AVS N, CVV N, 3DS not attempted, new account. Confident tone, zero evidence.

CB-2025-0005.why: Two invoices with different order IDs, items, auth codes, capture timestamps and DPD consignments. All three 12.6.1 requirements are on the page.

CB-2025-0006.why: Listing exists; the delivery photo is a front view and cannot prove the frame is sound; the returns policy exists but the issuer says the merchant ignored the refund request. Ask for the correspondence.

CB-2025-0007.why: Page 8 of the 10-page manifest: TF-9051 ref txn_7745MN collected from LS1 4DT and delivered to LS9 8AA on 22 Apr, before the 14 May chargeback.
CB-2025-0007.revised_because: The tool argued request_more_evidence because TerraFreight is itself the carrier, so the manifest is self-attestation, and the POD image it references was not supplied. That is a fair reading of 'tracking + carrier confirmation', so it is listed as acceptable. The designed test here was finding page 8 among nine pages of filler, and it did.

CB-2025-0008.why: Only the generic terms document. No opt-in record, no renewal notification (terms promise 5 days, the rule wants 7+), nothing rebutting the claimed 18 March cancellation. Policy is not proof.
CB-2025-0008.revised_because: I first wanted needs_review, but the output is a clean, actionable list of six specific records to request. An analyst can send that in seconds. Tier is about how much scrutiny the output needs, not how weak the merchant's case is.

CB-2025-0009.why: Booking, accepted non-refundable policy with a consent id, and a front desk log marking NO-SHOW: requirements 1-3 are met. But the confirmation says the rate was charged at booking on 12 March, while the disputed transaction is dated 26 April 11:00 UTC, before check-in and before the no-show was recorded.
CB-2025-0009.revised_because: I missed the charge-date inconsistency when writing this key; the tool found it. If a separate 215 EUR was taken in March this is a duplicate, so asking for the folio before representing is the better call.

CB-2025-0010.why: Visa 10.5 is non-representable under the rule regardless of evidence. The strong 3DS record and delivery confirmation are a distraction: the tool must read the rule, not the documents.
